message.content: Triangulation metrics are a way to measure how well different pieces of information line up with each other—think of it like checking if three sides of a triangle fit together. In the context of product and branch data, they help you see whether the results from separate analyses (for example, sales numbers, customer feedback, and inventory levels) agree or disagree. By looking at these metrics, you can spot inconsistencies, validate your data, and make more confident decisions about which products or branches are performing consistently or need attention.
